pc-develop-lib.meta.description: PC Develop Lib V2 provides reusable content registration, language data generation and tag data generation modules for Minecraft Fabric mod development.
pc-develop-lib.lead: Reusable content registration and data generation modules for Minecraft Fabric mod development.
pc-develop-lib.overview: PC Develop Lib V2 is a foundation library for Minecraft Fabric development. It encapsulates content registration, language data generation and tag data generation in independent modules for reuse across mod projects.
pc-develop-lib.features.1.title: Content registration
pc-develop-lib.features.1.description: Modules for registering items, blocks, item groups, points of interest and villagers.
pc-develop-lib.features.2.title: Language data generation
pc-develop-lib.features.2.description: The data generation entry point provides configuration examples for Chinese and English language factories.
pc-develop-lib.features.3.title: Tag data generation
pc-develop-lib.features.3.description: Example configurations cover item tags and point-of-interest type tags.
pc-develop-lib.steps.1.title: Review the project setup
pc-develop-lib.steps.1.description: The current source configuration uses Java 25, Minecraft 1.21.10 and Fabric. Consult the repository's build configuration to confirm the development requirements before use.
pc-develop-lib.steps.2.title: Explore registration examples
pc-develop-lib.steps.2.description: Consult the register module and accompanying test examples for the structure and usage of the registration modules.
pc-develop-lib.steps.3.title: Explore data generation
pc-develop-lib.steps.3.description: Review the language and tag configuration in PCDevelopLibDataGenerator.java and the accompanying examples for the data generation workflow.

piscescup-easy.meta.description: PiscesCup Easy is a Fabric mod for Minecraft player management, with whitelists, operator permissions and bans by player name, plus Chinese and English command feedback.
piscescup-easy.lead: Manage whitelists, operator permissions and bans through a unified command interface, with operations based on player names.
piscescup-easy.overview: PiscesCup Easy is a Fabric mod for Minecraft player management. It provides whitelist management, operator permissions, bans and language settings through a unified command interface. The README recommends server-side use.
piscescup-easy.features.1.title: Whitelist management
piscescup-easy.features.1.description: Add or remove whitelist entries by player name to manage server access.
piscescup-easy.features.2.title: Operators and bans
piscescup-easy.features.2.description: Manage operator permissions and player-name bans through a consistent set of administrative commands.
piscescup-easy.features.3.title: Language settings
piscescup-easy.features.3.description: View the current language setting and switch command feedback between Chinese and English.
piscescup-easy.steps.1.title: Read the usage guide
piscescup-easy.steps.1.description: Consult the README for environment requirements and command documentation, and confirm that the selected build is compatible with your Minecraft version.
piscescup-easy.steps.2.title: Manage the whitelist
piscescup-easy.steps.2.description: Execute the commands below with the required administrative permissions, replacing TestPlayer with the actual player name.
piscescup-easy.steps.3.title: Choose the message language
piscescup-easy.steps.3.description: Use the language-setting command to select zh_cn or en_us.
piscescup-easy.example.caption: Commands from the README
piscescup-easy.example.label: Player-management command example
piscescup-easy.example.code:
/pc_easy whitelist add TestPlayer
/pc_easy setting lang set en_us
more-advancements.meta.description: More Advancements is a Fabric mod that extends Minecraft's advancement system with exploration and activity objectives, with advancement text in Chinese and English.
more-advancements.lead: Extend Minecraft's advancement system with additional objectives for exploration and everyday activities.
more-advancements.overview: More Advancements adds Minecraft advancements and challenge objectives covering dimension exploration and everyday activities, with advancement text in Chinese and English.
more-advancements.features.1.title: Themed advancements
more-advancements.features.1.description: Generated advancement data is organized into adventure, End, husbandry, Minecraft and Nether categories.
more-advancements.features.2.title: Challenge objectives
more-advancements.features.2.description: Existing challenges include collecting heads, observing mobs through a spyglass and eating chorus fruit.
more-advancements.features.3.title: Chinese and English support
more-advancements.features.3.description: The repository includes zh_cn and en_us advancement titles and descriptions.
more-advancements.steps.1.title: Review project documentation
more-advancements.steps.1.description: Consult the README for the project's advancement extension goals and related documentation.
more-advancements.steps.2.title: Explore the advancements
more-advancements.steps.2.description: Consult the generated advancement data and corresponding language files for each challenge's title and description.
more-advancements.steps.3.title: Submit advancement suggestions
more-advancements.steps.3.description: Submit suggestions for additional advancements through GitHub Issues, following the README guidance.
commons-lib.meta.description: Commons Lib is a Java 21 utility library providing validation, common data structures and functional-programming components, with Maven dependency support.
commons-lib.lead: Reusable Java components for validation, common data structures and functional programming.
commons-lib.overview: Commons Lib is a Java 21 utility library providing validation, common data structures and functional-programming tools. Its loosely coupled modules support component reuse and can be added to projects through Maven.
commons-lib.features.1.title: Utilities and validation
commons-lib.features.1.description: String, array and comparison helpers, plus null, argument and state validation.
commons-lib.features.2.title: Structured values
commons-lib.features.2.description: Intervals, Pair, fixed-arity tuples, and simple and atomic counters.
commons-lib.features.3.title: Extended functional interfaces
commons-lib.features.3.description: Multi-argument, primitive-specialized and throwable interfaces, with currying, partial application and memoization.
commons-lib.steps.1.title: Configure the Java environment
commons-lib.steps.1.description: Confirm that the project uses Java 21 or a compatible later version.
commons-lib.steps.2.title: Configure the dependency
commons-lib.steps.2.description: Select the required version and the dependency format for your build tool, then copy the configuration into the project's build file.
commons-lib.steps.3.title: Review usage examples
commons-lib.steps.3.description: The README includes quick examples for naming conversions, intervals, counters, functions and Pair.

linq.title: LINQ for Java · PiscesCup
linq.description: LINQ for Java: an Enumerable query library for Java 25, featuring fluent queries, deferred execution and primitive-specialized sequences.
linq.lead: Composable data processing for Java collections and sequences using a LINQ query style.
linq.overview: LINQ for Java provides queries for Java collections and sequences through the Enumerable model. Methods such as where, select and orderBy compose data processing steps; many intermediate operations use deferred execution and run when results are enumerated or consumed.
linq.enumerablesIntro: Object sequences and specialized int, long and double sequences provide query entry points for the corresponding data types.
linq.objectDescription: Create sequences from arrays, collections or varargs, then filter, order, group and join objects.
linq.intDescription: Use Linq.ofInts for int-specific queries and numeric aggregation such as sum and average.
linq.longDescription: Use Linq.ofLongs for long-valued data, reducing unnecessary boxing and unboxing in primitive pipelines.
linq.doubleDescription: Use Linq.ofDoubles for filtering, transforming and aggregating double-valued data.
linq.features.filterDescription: Filter elements with where, transform results with select, and control sequence ranges with skip and take.
linq.features.orderDescription: Combine orderBy and thenBy for multi-level sorting, and use groupBy to group elements by key.
linq.features.joinDescription: Correlate sequences with join and groupJoin; use distinct, union, intersect and except for deduplication and set operations.
linq.features.aggregateDescription: Consume results with operators such as count, first and aggregate, or materialize them as lists, arrays and maps.
linq.prepareDescription: The repository README and compiler configuration require JDK 25 or later.
linq.installDescription: Select a build tool and copy the dependency configuration example. Version 1.0.0 is taken from the repository's pom.xml; confirm publication or follow the README to build and install it in a local repository before use.
linq.sampleDescription: Filter even numbers, calculate their squares, and retrieve the query results with toArray.
linq.relatedDescription: Related projects include the Commons Lib utility dependency and the separate linq-in-java repository.

examples.heading: Code examples
examples.runHint: Expand an example to view its complete Java class and output. Configure the dependency, save the code with the displayed filename, and run the main method. After selecting a different dependency version, check its compatibility with the version used by the examples.
examples.source: View this example in the README
examples.commons.intro: This section presents five examples adapted from Quick Examples in the Commons Lib README, with main methods and output statements added. Compilation and output were verified with Commons Lib 1.1.6.
examples.commons.namingDescription: Use StringUtils to convert between snake_case, UpperCamel and lowerCamel naming styles.
examples.commons.intervalDescription: Create a closed-open [1, 10) interval with IntInterval and check its boundaries and formatted representation.
examples.commons.counterDescription: Create a counter with Counter.atomic, increment and add to it, then read its current value.
examples.commons.functionDescription: Calculate volume with TriFunction, using full invocation, partial application and memorized result caching.
examples.commons.pairDescription: Transform the left-hand string with mappedLeft while preserving the right-hand Integer value.
examples.linq.intro: This section presents six queries from the LINQ for Java README, with imports, main methods and required record definitions added. The examples were compiled and run against repository version 1.0.0 with JDK 25. Refer to the dependency section for publication status.
examples.linq.filterDescription: Create an Int sequence with Linq.ofInts, filter even numbers with where, and retrieve the results with toArray.
examples.linq.projectionDescription: Use select and String::length to map names to their string lengths and collect the results into a List.
examples.linq.orderingDescription: Apply multi-level sorting by age and then name. Person.toString retains the README output format; the optional annotation is omitted.
examples.linq.aggregationDescription: Calculate the sum and average with IntEnumerable's sum and average methods. The example corrects the README output label age to avg.
examples.linq.setsDescription: Use distinct, except, intersect and union for unique values, difference, intersection and union.
examples.linq.studentsDescription: Based on the README Student example, select students with scores of at least 80, order by descending score, and extract their names.
